thread:
maria: Quick heads-up — after today's packing refactor I see a noticeable p95 regression on INT8 weight-only (AWQ) workloads. Running local perf harness on g5.12x: 

maria: Baseline (fp16): batch=8, seq=256 => p50=32ms p95=120ms
maria: INT8 AWQ (group=128, packing enabled): batch=8, seq=256 => p50=28ms p95=150ms (p95 +25%)
maria: Microprofile shows an extra ~0.9ms per request in pack/unpack when KV cache is cold; when KV warm the penalty is smaller but still nontrivial.

ravi: thanks — can you paste the perf output + flame? Was this after the kernel selection change?

maria: pasted below (truncated):
```
# perf-run --model gpt-3-small --quant awq --group 128 --batch 8 --seq 256
Total tokens: 1e6
Avg latency: 34.1ms
P50: 28.3ms P95: 149.8ms
Top stacks (time%):
  pack_unpacked_loop  21%  
  matmul_int8_kernel   18%
  kv_lookup            12%
  kv_cache_miss_copy   9%
```

maria: flame shows a hot path in pack_unpacked_loop where we memcpy into prepacked buffer per request; previous impl did a single copy for the whole batch. Looks like the refactor moved pack to per-request to avoid synchronization but added memcpy cost.

lucy: hmm. packing cost interacts badly with small sequence lengths and high concurrency. Two levers: reduce group size (fewer quant groups => less pack work) or change pack threshold so we do batch-wide pack when batch_size>1.

lucy: suggestion heuristics: 
- if batch_size >= 4 -> do batch pack once and share prepacked tensors
- if avg_seq_len < 128 -> group_size = min(64, default_group)

ravi: we also saw kernel selector occasionally picking fp16 fallback for some matmuls when quant calibration variance > 0.12 (we changed threshold in the selector last week). That could explain p95 tails if some requests hit slower fp16 kernels intermittently.

perf-bot: automatic summary: commit abc1234 (+pack-refactor) correlated with +22% p95 on int8-awq group=128 tests. Linked CI run: https://ci/reports/1755

simon: I bisected — commit abc1234 is the refactor that moved packing into request path to reduce lock contention. Short term we can revert that specific change or gate it behind a heuristic. Longer term we need a lock-free batch pack path.

devon: I'll run microbench across group sizes [32,64,128,256] and post numbers. Also test pack-as-batch flag. Will try to reproduce on dedicated infra (nvlink config).

maria: action items:
- devon: run microbench and open PR with (a) pack threshold heuristic and (b) option to do batch pack when batch_size>1. Target: small PR by EOD tomorrow.
- lucy & ravi: propose updated kernel selection threshold for fp16 fallback — try bumping allowed calibration variance from 0.12 -> 0.15 and measure downstream quality drop.
- simon: add a short-lived perf test that runs AWQ int8 p95 baseline nightly to catch regressions earlier.

ravi: one more note on KV cache: when KV cold we see extra copies because prepacked buffers are allocated lazily per-request. If we preallocate and reuse for duration of batch lifetime we can save ~0.6ms per req. But we need to avoid memory blowup for large groups.

maria: agreed. Please add memory usage curve to the microbench results. If group=256 + prealloc, watch resident size.

devon: starting runs now. Will ping with results in this thread. :rocket:

maria: thanks everyone. Keeping this thread as the single source for triage — feel free to @mention if you need unblock.
